summary: Specializing in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Kuntala Bhattacharya studied under MA supervisor Prabal Kumar Sen and earned a PhD from Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra (attested 2009). Bhattacharya held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).
Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Patrul Rinpoche (~1880–1887). He taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
summary: Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).

Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kuo-Pin Chuang earned a Ph.D. from National Chung Hsing University. Posts include postdoctoral researcher at National Taiwan University (2019–2022) and the University of Edinburgh (2022), and professor at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Kurt A. Behrendt earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1991–1997). At the Metropolitan Museum of Art, he was Assistant Curator of Asian Art (~2004–2014) and Associate Curator of South Asian Art (~2014).
Working in Indology and other fields, Kurt Andrew Johnson earned his PhD at the University of York under the supervision of Jane Moody, completing it by 2010.
In the field of Buddhist studies, Kurt Bruno Otto Fischer studied as a pupil under Paul Dahlke (~1920–1928). He succeeded Dahlke in 1928 and served as leader at Das Buddhistische Haus (~1928–1942).

Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Leidecker earned his B.A. from Oberlin College (~1921–1924) and Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1924–1927). He held professorships at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1934–1942), Lehigh University (1948), and University of Mary Washington (1948–1973).

Kurt Huber studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and earned a PhD from the University of Munich (~1913–1917), where he taught Hans Hartog. In philosophy, he held an außerordentlicher Professor post (1926) and a Professur (1938) at the University of Munich.
Active in religious studies and Indology, Kurt Hutten completed his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen (~1926–1930), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (~1927–1930).

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Klemm studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1889–1893) under Albrecht Weber, Karl Friedrich Geldner, and Johannes Schmidt. He completed a PhD at the University of Leipzig (~1891–1894) under Ernst Windisch and Karl Brugmann.
Kurt Quecke was a scholar in Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Marburg under doctoral supervisor Johannes Nobel, finishing by 1947.
Working in Buddhist studies, Kurt Schmidt obtained a Dr. iuris at the University of Rostock (~1899–1901) and founded the Buddhistische Arbeitsgemeinschaft in 1946.

Linguist Kurt Stegmann von Pritzwald studied at Munich and Giessen (1920–1925) and earned a Ph.D. under Albert Debrunner at Jena (~1925–1928). He held academic posts at Jena, Kiel, Rostock, and Marburg, where he became apl. Professor in 1945.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Tropper studied at the University of Vienna under Michael Torsten Much, Tashi Geisler, and Ernst Steinkellner, earning a doctorate by 2001. His posts include Vertragsassistent at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

In linguistics and sinology, Wulff studied at Copenhagen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He served at Thesaurus Linguae Latinae (1906–1918) and the Royal Danish Library (1918), before holding posts at the University of Copenhagen as Privatdozent (1920), Lecturer (1926), and Docent (1928).

In the field of Indology, Kurt von Kamptz earned his Ph.D. at the University of Hamburg (~1924–1929), studying under Walther Schubring (~1925–1929). He later served as a librarian at Wehrkreisbücherei IV Dresden.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Schaeffer studied at Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, Washington, and Harvard (PhD, ~1995–2000). He held posts as assistant and associate professor at the University of Alabama (2000, 2004) and joined the University of Virginia (2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, serving as head at the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested 1998) and holding a post there (attested 2009).
